title: Polymer clay faux jasper stone pendant
subtitle: Swirled red and brown tones imitating the banded pattern of jasper
excerpt: Red jasper's irregular swirling pattern is created in polymer clay by partially mixing a terracotta red with dark brown and ivory, then cutting a flat stone-shaped pendant from the result. Incomplete mixing is the technique: the colours should bleed into each other but not fully combine. No kiln is required.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Faux-stone polymer clay methods are a widely documented craft technique.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling material that cures hard in a domestic oven at 110 to 130°C

content.text: Jasper is a mineral with irregular swirling patterns of red, brown, yellow, and cream. The key to imitating it in
is partial mixing: fold and twist the colours together just enough to create veining but stop before the colours blend into one muddy tone. No kiln is required.
Condition each colour separately. Roll into logs of roughly equal length and twist all three logs together in a loose spiral.
Fold the twisted log in half and roll into a log again. Repeat the fold and roll 4 to 5 times only. More than 6 folds risks overblending the colours.

Slice across the log to check the veining pattern. The cut face should show distinct swirls and veins of the three colours. If it looks too uniform, the mixing has gone too far; start with fresh clay next time.
Roll the partially mixed clay to 5 mm thick. Cut an irregular oval or pebble shape about 4 cm by 3 cm: no perfectly geometric edges, as natural jasper is rarely symmetrical.
Pierce a hanging hole at the top with the needle tool. Place on a ceramic tile.
Cure at 130°C for 30 minutes. Ventilate the kitchen. Cool fully before handling.
Sand from 400 to 800 grit under water for a polished stone look. Buff dry. Attach a bail through the pierced hole.
Use yellow, orange, and brown tones for a yellow jasper look. Use grey, blue, and white for a chalcedony or agate effect.

items.problem: Colours have blended into a uniform muddy terracotta
items.cause: Too many fold cycles overworked the colour boundaries
items.fix: Start fresh with new clay. A good jasper mix takes 4 to 6 folds at most. Lay out a test slice after 4 folds before continuing

items.problem: Pendant surface shows cracks after sanding
items.cause: Clay was not fully conditioned before mixing, leaving stress in the body
items.fix: Sand lightly through finer grits only. Fill any visible cracks with a tiny amount of raw clay pressed in, then re-cure for 10 minutes before sanding again
